title: Beyond Solution-Centric Search: Adaptive Inquiry and Knowledge Revision for Autonomous ML Engineering
publication_status: arXiv preprint, submitted 2026-08-03; peer-reviewed venue not verified

claims.claim: Research uses a fixed development evaluator; the formal objective reserves a protected held-out evaluation for the final solution.
claims.use: Match evidence and final selection rules; no local result implied.

claims.claim: Knowledge consists of scoped claims, positive/negative evidence pointers and active/qualified/invalidated status, updated across experiments.
claims.use: Direct prior-art overlap: scoped evidence and invalidation alone are not a novelty claim.

claims.claim: Epistemic actions diagnose decision-critical unknowns without changing the retained solution; interventional actions create candidate solutions.
claims.use: Mechanism distinction is not the local R1/R2 authorization distinction; training or selection scores remain R1.

claims.claim: Main benchmark comparators are source/leaderboard reported; cross-domain optimizers use different backbones despite other matched conditions.
claims.use: Do not infer isolated harness superiority or compare reported SOTA scores across unmatched protocols.

claims.claim: Component ablations run once on each of 15 small-data tasks; information-management removal also removes persistent knowledge and multigranularity retrieval.
claims.use: Not a pure graph-versus-equally-capable non-graph contrast; supports a matched-information control.

claims.claim: Trajectory analysis reports multiple private-test scores; whether these are post-hoc rescoring or feedback is not specified in this passage.
claims.use: Reading uncertainty, not an accusation of leakage; do not import an online test-score trajectory into local primary protocol.
